items.headline: PHP critical security release due 19 Nov 14:00-14:30 UTC; not yet published at 13:07 UTC
items.summary: PHP's security team pre-announced releases for all supported branches rated CRITICAL, needing non-default or uncommon setups. CVE-2026-115560 is expected. As of 13:07 UTC no fixed versions or full CVE list had been published on php.net.
items.label: VENDOR-ACKNOWLEDGED
items.labelBasis: The scheduled release and its CRITICAL rating come from the PHP security team's own php.net notice of 18 Nov; CVE-2026-115560 conditions are from its 23 Oct advisory. Fixed versions, CVE list and release itself are unconfirmed so far.
items.firstReported: 22:38 on 18 Nov (The Register); php.net notice dated 18 Nov, time not shown

sections.happened: On 18 November the PHP security team announced releases for all supported branches (8.2 to 8.5), scheduled for 19 November between 14:00 and 14:30 UTC, saying the highest severity is CRITICAL. The notice said technical details and fixed version numbers will be published alongside the releases. As of 13:07 UTC (13:07 UK time) on 19 November, php.net still listed 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 as current, and its release feed showed no newer release; no CVE list, fixed versions or full advisory had been published. Aikido, updating its page on 19 November, said the same. The release follows the 21 October PHP2Shell fixes (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619); PHP 8.6.0 GA was also planned for 19 November.
sections.technical: Only one issue is identified: CVE-2026-115560, a remote code execution vector in session upload progress. Per PHP's 23 October advisory, exploitation needs session.serialize_handler set to php_binary or php_serialize in configuration, runtime ini_set() switching it to php before session_start(), and session upload progress enabled (the default). Applications that never change the handler at runtime are not described as exposed. Affected versions, CVSS score and weakness class have not been published; the 21 October releases do not fix it. The other CRITICAL issues are unnamed. No exploitation of CVE-2026-115560 has been reported in the sources read.
sections.guidance: PHP's security team (23 October advisory) suggested setting session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until the next regular bugfix release; the setting must apply before request parsing, so ini_set() and .user.ini do not work. Its 18 November notice said users are strongly encouraged to prepare to upgrade promptly once releases appear. No fixed version numbers exist yet.
sections.differing: PHP Foundation executive director Elizabeth Barron told The Register in October the flaw needs a very unlikely configuration and application-code combination not expected in practical use, so it received no emergency fix. PHP nonetheless rates the November issues CRITICAL. Vendors such as Aikido describe the mitigation as sufficient for this CVE only, not for other issues in the release.
sections.unknown: Fixed version numbers, the full CVE list, CVSS scores, which other issues are rated CRITICAL, and whether the release lands inside the 14:00-14:30 UTC window remain unpublished.

items.headline: CISA adds four exploited flaws to KEV catalog: Synology DSM, LiteLLM, Apache Axis, REDCap
items.summary: CISA added four flaws to its KEV catalog on 18 November 2026: Synology DSM, BerriAI LiteLLM, Apache Axis and Vanderbilt REDCap. Federal deadlines: 21 November (Synology, Axis, REDCap) and 2 December (LiteLLM).
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: CISA catalog listing; several outlets report the same four entries
items.firstReported: 18 November 2026 (US Wednesday); first source CISA alert, not read; exact UK time not confirmed

sections.happened: On 18 November 2026 CISA added four vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, citing evidence of active exploitation: Synology DSM (CVE-2024-10441), BerriAI LiteLLM (CVE-2026-40217), Apache Axis (CVE-2026-90436) and Vanderbilt REDCap (CVE-2026-90817).
sections.technical: Synology DSM (CVE-2024-10441): improper output encoding in the system plugin daemon (catalog text cites BeeStation OS); remote code execution. LiteLLM (CVE-2026-40217): code execution via bytecode rewriting at /guardrails/test_custom_code. Apache Axis (CVE-2026-90436): unsafe reflection via a crafted SOAP fault, unauthenticated; CISA says the product may be end-of-life. REDCap (CVE-2026-90817): unauthenticated code injection via a public survey context; requires a valid public survey hash.
sections.guidance: CISA: apply mitigations per vendor instructions. BOD 26-04 deadlines apply to federal agencies; CISA encourages all organisations to use the KEV catalog to prioritise remediation.
sections.differing: LiteLLM access: shattered.io, citing Beam, says exploitation needs a proxy-admin credential; The Hacker News, citing Google Threat Intelligence Group, says attackers used it to turn limited-access inference keys into full admin credentials. Ransomware: CISA lists ransomware use as unknown for all four; The Hacker News reports Synology disclosed CVE-2024-10441 exploitation in C3RB3R ransomware attacks. LiteLLM CVSS: NVD 8.8 (CVSS 3.1) versus GitHub 5.9 (CVSS v4), as reported by shattered.io.
sections.unknown: Threat actors behind the exploitation are not named. Victim counts are not published. Vendor advisories were not read.

items.headline: Malicious Microsoft Agent Framework PyPI releases 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 steal cloud and CI credentials
items.summary: Two trojanised releases of Microsoft's agent-framework package (about 190,000 monthly downloads) were uploaded to PyPI on 17 November and quarantined within about 40 minutes. A startup hook harvested Azure, GitHub Actions and CI/CD credentials. How the attacker gained publishing access is unconfirmed.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: A Microsoft maintainer confirmed on GitHub that the compromised versions were pulled and an investigation is under way; a Microsoft spokesperson commented to The Register; Wiz, Upwind, StepSecurity, Socket, JFrog and others independently analysed the same malware.
items.firstReported: 17 Nov 2026: upload 20:35 UTC (= 20:35 GMT, UK time); GitHub issue by Upwind and OpenSourceMalware report by 21:43 UTC; BleepingComputer and Help Net Security followed 18-19 Nov

sections.happened: Two malicious releases of Microsoft's agent-framework Python package, 1.26.1 and 1.26.2, were uploaded to PyPI on 17 November 2026 at 20:35 and 21:08 UTC (identical to UK time, GMT). The package is the meta-package for Microsoft Agent Framework, with roughly 190,000 monthly downloads. StepSecurity reports PyPI quarantined 1.26.1 at 21:06 UTC and 1.26.2 at 21:16 UTC; 1.26.0, published 12 November, is the last clean release. A Microsoft maintainer commented on the GitHub issue that the compromised versions were pulled and an investigation was under way. On 18 November a Microsoft spokesperson told The Register some repositories were made private "while we investigate malicious content"; the agent-framework repository was offline.
sections.technical: Wheel-only uploads added a .pth startup hook (T1546.018) that launches a detached process on every Python start, without importing the package: agent_framework_meta.pth in 1.26.1, af_runtime_diag.pth and .py in 1.26.2. It collects matching environment variables, up to 60 credential files (80 in 1.26.2) and other processes' /proc environ (T1552.001), and requests Azure managed-identity, Azure DevOps OIDC and, in 1.26.2, GitHub Actions OIDC tokens (T1552.005, T1528). One zlib/base64 POST goes to webhook[.]site/d381fd80-ec62-42ad-8f5c-d1b15103c9bb (T1567). Other IOCs: User-Agents af-runtime-diagnostics/1 and runtime-diagnostics/1, env _AF_TEL=1, wheel SHA-256 d27fa344…e110 and 3d20a8bc…e0a9. No CVE; vector T1195.002.
sections.guidance: Microsoft's maintainer stated the compromised versions were pulled from the package feed; no separate Microsoft advisory or CVE was found. Upwind's GitHub report names 1.26.0 as clean and says setting _AF_TEL=1 or running python -S prevents execution. Wiz, OX Security and StepSecurity publish pinning, credential-rotation and log-review steps.
sections.differing: Root cause disputed. Wiz says a Microsoft ESRP client certificate and key appear compromised, publishing from Microsoft-owned IP space. Upwind and JFrog say the wheels were hand-repacked outside the release pipeline, likely via a stolen PyPI credential. SafeDep suspects new PyPI maintainer vibiret; unconfirmed. The Register's subheading cites a GitHub org admin compromise without evidence. Microsoft has confirmed none.
sections.unknown: How publishing access was obtained; whether it is revoked and vibiret removed; install and victim counts (Wiz found three successful victim exfiltrations among 50 retained requests); attribution (tooling self-identified as Cairn; no actor named); why other Microsoft repositories went private.

items.headline: Optimizely signup flaw used to inject skimmer and iOS exploit code into sites of 178 organisations
items.summary: On 16 November an attacker abused a flaw in Optimizely's Web Experimentation signup flow to add malicious JavaScript to customer projects. Report URI found it in snippets tied to 178 organisations; Optimizely says the flaw is fixed and fewer than 5% of customers were affected.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Optimizely acknowledged the exploit on its status page and in an incident report; Report URI independently captured the infected files; multiple outlets corroborate.
items.firstReported: 16 Nov 2026 22:47 UTC (Report URI blog; UK time = UTC in November); Optimizely status notice 17 Nov 01:02 UTC; Krebs on Security 17 Nov

sections.happened: On 16 November 2026 malicious JavaScript was served through Optimizely Web Experimentation snippets to visitors of sites run by 178 organisations, including the BBC, CNN, Zoom, Salesforce, GitLab, IKEA, HSBC, Equifax and Ledger, according to Report URI. It found the code in 188 of 1,611 snippets it examined and says the true count is likely higher. Optimizely posted a notice at 01:02 UTC on 17 November, then an incident report. An 18 November update says fewer than 5% of customers were affected and no malicious code remains. Report URI recorded about $7,040 received by attacker wallets by 19:25 UTC on 16 November.
sections.technical: Per Optimizely, the attacker created accounts through the signup flow (from 00:37 UTC, some IPs commercial VPN), exploited a flaw to impersonate administrators using public information and brute force, then edited Project JavaScript. Files still came from cdn.optimizely.com. Report URI: loader pulled 1688360.cc/track.js (plain, base64 or inline fallback), rebuilt 26 times; it swapped crypto addresses, skimmed card details typed into page forms (hosted iframes out of reach), and sent cookies and screenshots. On iPhones and iPads, boot.js from 5vobauua3ojpklx.icu and eil786npto9u5bq.icu loaded Coruna (iOS 13–17) or DarkSword (iOS 18.x) kits. No CVE assigned. Analyst ATT&CK mapping: T1195, T1189. Actor unnamed.
sections.guidance: Optimizely states it closed the signup flaw at 16:10 UTC, removed injected code by 22:24 UTC, ended sessions, revoked tokens, reset affected accounts and engaged Mandiant; per-site exposure windows are available via customer success managers. Report URI says the kit's comments treat iOS 18.7.3 and later, and 26.3 and later, as patched.
sections.differing: Start time: Optimizely puts the first malicious write at 07:51 UTC; Report URI saw the BBC snippet injected at 04:21 UTC, and Hudson Rock 04:31 UTC. Archived captures favour the earlier time; Optimizely has not reconciled it. Loss figures: Report URI $7,040 (16 Nov); Krebs about $7,500. Helme's China-origin speculation is unverified.
sections.unknown: Visitor, card and cookie exposure counts; whether any iOS exploit succeeded (none reported); actor identity; reason for the start-time gap; how Optimizely's under-5% of customers relates to 178 organisations; Mandiant findings; links to earlier Kissmetrics, StorifyMe and minute-ly injections.

items.summary: The Gentlemen ransomware group listed NVIDIA on its leak site on 18 November 2026 with a countdown and no sample data. NVIDIA says its systems show no sign of compromise and it is probing a third-party partner.
items.label: UNCONFIRMED CLAIM
items.labelBasis: Group's leak-site listing only; no data published; NVIDIA denies its own systems affected.
items.firstReported: Wed 18 November 2026 (UK time not stated in sources); first reports from BleepingComputer, Cybernews and Newsweek, 19 November

sections.happened: The Gentlemen ransomware-as-a-service group added NVIDIA to its dark-web leak site on 18 November 2026, with a countdown to an alleged release of 'SOON' data. No files were published. NVIDIA told BleepingComputer it is investigating an incident that may have affected a third-party partner.
sections.technical: No technical details have been published: no intrusion date, affected business unit, data type or samples. Tracker classifies the entry as pending. The group is described as double-extortion ransomware; no ATT&CK mapping for this claim is available.
sections.differing: The group's listing implies it holds company data. NVIDIA says it found no indication its systems or networks were affected. Analyst Aras Nazarovas (Cybernews) expects misattributed or minor data.
sections.unknown: Whether any data was taken, from NVIDIA or a partner, and whether the 28 November deadline will bring a leak.

items.headline: Google/Mandiant: Russian group Cold Relic (Star Blizzard) reused data from one US cloud breach to compromise another
items.summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant report that Cold Relic, a group the US DOJ has assessed as FSB-linked, used data and identities stolen from a US organisation in late 2025 to phish a second US organisation in 2026. Neither victim is named.
items.label: VENDOR-ACKNOWLEDGED
items.labelBasis: Rests on one primary report by Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant, which responded to both intrusions; press coverage repeats it. Neither victim has been named or has commented, and no independent technical evidence has been published, such as indicators of compromise.

sections.happened: Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) and Mandiant published a case study on 17 November 2026 (page metadata: 22:11–23:59 UTC, i.e. GMT) on the Russian group COLD RELIC, formerly COLDRIVER/UNC4057, also known as Star Blizzard, Callisto and Gossamer Bear. Mandiant investigated a late-2025 intrusion at one US organisation and a 2026 intrusion at a second. In the second, the actor impersonated an employee of the first victim over an encrypted messaging app, using data likely taken in the first breach. Neither organisation is named. GTIG says it saw new COLD RELIC phishing as recently as November 2026. Google cites a US Department of Justice assessment that the group operates within Russia's FSB.
sections.technical: Case 1 (late 2025): stolen Google Workspace Super Admin credentials, a residential proxy near the victim, and an MFA push-fatigue attack (T1621). The actor registered an unseen device, passkeys, backup codes and rogue MFA devices (T1098.005); bulk-downloaded Drive (T1530, T1567.002); ran a Customer Takeout export (T1119); and deleted Alert Center items (T1562.008). Access lasted months, including OAuth mail sync (T1114.002) and passkeys that survived password and session resets. Case 2 (2026): phishing links, via compromised-site redirectors, sent over the messaging app harvested Entra ID credentials and tokens. Entra ID federates SSO to Google Workspace. The actor added an MFA device and bulk-downloaded one user's Drive. No malware or CVE is reported, and no IOCs are published.
sections.guidance: Google/GTIG lists these mitigations: phishing-resistant FIDO2 keys, auditing passkey and MFA device registrations, revoking sessions, OAuth tokens and unauthorised passkeys in addition to password resets, residential-proxy IP reputation feeds, cloud DLP rules, and auditing OAuth grants. It also publishes Workspace detection mappings to ATT&CK, and issues government-backed attack alerts to targeted Google accounts.
sections.differing: No dispute is reported. Russia has not publicly responded in the sources reviewed. The FSB attribution comes from a US DOJ assessment that Google cites, and Google's own technical link between the two intrusions is stated as likely: a June 2026 VirusTotal redirector URL referencing the first victim and the impersonation pretext.
sections.unknown: Identities and sectors of both victims, what data was taken, and how widely the stolen data has been reused. Google did not name the messaging app used, or say whether the actor's later persona reached other organisations.

items.headline: Run of US outages (Microsoft, FAA, Chase, Apple, NSA network) prompts resilience debate; officials cite maintenance, no attack
items.summary: Between 12 and 17 November, Microsoft 365, FAA air traffic communications, JPMorgan Chase, Apple and the NSA's classified NSANet each failed. Each operator cited software or maintenance faults; officials report no evidence of cyberattack or of linkage. Debate centres on AI-driven patching.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Each outage was acknowledged by the affected operator (Microsoft, FAA, JPMorgan Chase, Apple, NSA), with FAA and Microsoft publishing cause details. The claimed common cause (AI-driven patch surge) is inference, not confirmed.
items.firstReported: 12 Nov 2026 (Microsoft 365, 16:20 UK) to 17 Nov 2026 (NSA, Apple); resilience coverage 17-19 Nov

sections.happened: Between 12 and 17 November, several US outages occurred. Microsoft 365 (Outlook, Exchange Online, Teams) was disrupted for about 24 hours from 16:20 UK on 12 November. The FAA ordered a nationwide departure ground stop at about 20:30 UK on 13 November, lifted at 01:15 UK on 14 November; it reported 12,462 cancellations, not all caused by the stop. Workday was unavailable that evening. JPMorgan Chase had a transaction disruption on 16 November. On 17 November Apple's iCloud, App Store and other services failed after an "internal update", and the NSA's classified NSANet became intermittent, with staggered staff arrivals at Fort Meade continuing on 18 November. Officials say there is no evidence of a cyberattack.
sections.technical: Microsoft's preliminary report: a July gateway-server update bug, extra traffic after a Teams failover and about 14% capacity offline left over 80% of servers unresponsive. FAA: legacy equipment destabilised by data flooding the FTI network at 1,000 connection attempts every 4-5 seconds, traced to an Amarillo, Texas radar site and an El Dorado, Arkansas radio site where L3Harris had deployed a new router; 17 of 22 en-route centres affected. Chase: a software bug in on-premise hardware. Apple: internal update. NSA: scheduled routine maintenance; DNI Jay Clayton linked it to patching PHP vulnerabilities found with AI tools. No CVEs, actor or IOCs published for the outages.
sections.guidance: Per FAA: L3Harris blocked the two sites, broadcast function disabled on new routers, and new router installations paused (reported by Fox Business). Per Microsoft: capacity increased, monitoring improved, safeguards added; final report expected. Per The Record, FBI cyber teams are assisting FAA, DOT and L3Harris. Sen. Schumer asked for a red-team review by 1 December.
sections.differing: Clayton, Rubio and Sen. Warner say the incidents are separate maintenance or patching failures, not coordinated or state-sponsored. Schumer calls the timing "too coincidental". Duffy blamed the contractor or router; the FAA says legacy equipment, not upgrades. Rapid7's Christiaan Beek says public evidence does not show rushed patches caused outages. Operator statements are better supported than the linkage theory.
sections.unknown: Root causes remain open for the FAA routers (replicated in a Florida lab, per CNBC sources), NSANet and Apple. NSA has not itself confirmed the PHP link. Full NSANet restoration time is unclear. Whether AI-driven patching contributed is unverified.

items.headline: Ukraine and FBI arrest four ransomware members tied to $40.5m in ransoms
items.summary: Ukraine's National Police and Prosecutor General's Office say four key members of a ransomware organisation were detained after a two-year probe with the FBI. Police say at least 28 companies paid over $40.5m; initial access came via fake IT-support calls.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Ukraine's National Police and Prosecutor General's Office both published the arrests, suspect notices and figures; reported by multiple outlets. FBI participation is stated by Ukrainian authorities; no FBI or US DoJ statement found. Payment totals and victim details are police or court-record allegations.

sections.happened: Ukraine's National Police published the case on 18 November 2026 (10:30 UK) via an interview with acting chief Maksym Tsutskiridze on Censor.NET; the Prosecutor General's Office issued a parallel statement. Police say Cyber Police and investigators worked with the FBI for over two years, ran 66 simultaneous searches in Kyiv and 11 regions, and seized equipment, bank cards, nearly $370,000 and €20,000. Four key members were served suspicion notices and remanded in custody. Police say at least 28 companies paid over $40.5m (about UAH 1.8bn); total damage is still being established. The organisation has at least 27 members from several countries including Ukraine and Russia; a wider 60+ person network in eight jurisdictions includes ex-Conti members. Maximum sentence: 15 years.
sections.technical: Police describe voice phishing: callers posed as IT support and obtained credentials or remote-access installs (ATT&CK T1566.004, T1219, T1078; mapping is this brief's). Tsutskiridze said the group built a platform using AI-generated voice messages. Attackers then stole data, encrypted files and threatened publication (T1486). Per Ukrainian court records reported by LeMagIT and BleepingComputer: ransomware named is Chaos; fake corporate-VPN pages, TeamViewer and AnyDesk were used; at Warren Oil a two-factor code was obtained after credential entry (T1111). Alleged payments: Warren Oil 84.5 BTC (about $5m, August 2024), Newpark $1.5m (December 2024), Quantum Health $5m (June 2026, after a $15m demand). No CVEs or IOCs published.
sections.differing: Police say the wider network includes ex-Conti members but have not said the four detainees were, or tied them to BlackSuit or Chaos (per BleepingComputer). BlackSuit claimed Maxxis International in November 2024, while court records name Chaos. Police's unnamed US victim (1.4 TB, $5m paid) matches Warren Oil's figures, but no source confirms they are the same case.
sections.unknown: Suspects' names, arrest locations and roles are undisclosed. Ransomware brand(s) used remain unconfirmed. No FBI or DoJ statement found. BleepingComputer's article body was unreadable; its details come from search excerpts.

items.headline: Russian national charged with spying on defence tech firm's employees; media identify firm as Palantir
items.summary: US prosecutors charged Igor D'iu, a Russian national, with acting as a foreign agent in a Russian-directed surveillance and stalking campaign against employees of a defence tech firm over its Ukraine work.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: DOJ/FBI charges and statements; company named by media sources, not by DOJ.
items.firstReported: 18 Nov 2026 (US time), DOJ announcement reported by The Hill; UK time not confirmed

sections.happened: Igor D'iu was arrested 30 October and charged with conspiracy to act as a foreign government agent, interstate stalking and identity document fraud. Prosecutors say Russia recruited and funded him to surveil employees of a Palo Alto defence technology firm. Bloomberg and others identify the firm as Palantir.
sections.technical: Non-cyber. Court filings allege D'iu photographed employees' laptop screens at cafes, carried a laptop and Wi-Fi equipment his handlers could control remotely, and held dossiers on employees and their families. The filings do not say whether any employee data was obtained.
sections.differing: The Record says Palantir did not respond to comment requests. Media attribution to Palantir rests on unnamed sources; the DOJ indictment does not name the company.
sections.unknown: Whether any employee data was obtained is not stated. The handlers have not been publicly identified.

sections.happened: On 18 Nov 2026 Palo Alto Networks (NASDAQ: PANW) said it entered a definitive agreement to acquire Applied Compute, a post-training and inference platform for open-weight AI models. The all-stock deal is valued at $4.5bn, subject to adjustments, and is expected to close in fiscal Q3 2027 pending regulatory clearance. items.headline: Echo study: three AI models agree on one of 121 potential code flaws
items.summary: Security firm Echo compared Claude Mythos 5.1, GPT-5.6 Sol and GLM-5.3 auditing the same open-source code. Of 121 potential issues, one was found by all three; 83% by a single model.
items.label: VENDOR-ACKNOWLEDGED
items.labelBasis: Vendor's own research; no maintainer confirmation; projects unnamed.
items.firstReported: 18 Nov 2026 (Echo research and press release, via AI Journal); Infosecurity Magazine followed

sections.happened: Echo, a software security firm, published research on 18 November comparing Anthropic's Claude Mythos 5.1, OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol and Z.ai's GLM-5.3 auditing two Maven libraries and one npm package. Of 121 potential issues, 83% came from one model. Projects remain unnamed pending maintainer notification.
sections.technical: Nine runs produced 446 findings, cut to 152; 74 rated High or Critical; 55 underwent automated proof-of-concept testing, 42 passed. Echo says the 42 may not be distinct bugs. Medium and Low findings were not tested.
sections.differing: Severity split on one npm flaw: GLM-5.3 Critical, Mythos High, GPT-5.6 Sol documented behaviour, validation Low. Echo's cost figures reflect its own access terms.
sections.unknown: Maintainer confirmation, affected project names and technical details are unpublished. Echo calls it a single controlled comparison, not a benchmark.

items.headline: Scattered Spider member Tyler Buchanan sentenced to six years for phishing, SIM swaps and crypto theft
items.summary: A UK national, Tyler Robert Buchanan, was sentenced in US federal court to 72 months for text-message phishing, SIM-swap and crypto theft linked to Scattered Spider. Restitution hearing set for 11 December.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: US Justice Department press release and two reporting outlets; sentence confirmed by DOJ.
items.firstReported: 18 Nov 2026, 00:09 UK time (DOJ release dated 17 Nov, 19:09 US Eastern); first outlet report followed

sections.happened: Tyler Robert Buchanan, 24, of Dundee, Scotland, was sentenced on 17 November 2026 by Judge John W. Holcomb in Santa Ana, California, to 72 months in federal prison. He pleaded guilty in April to conspiracy to commit wire fraud and aggravated identity theft. He is the fifth and final defendant sentenced. Restitution hearing is set for 11 December.
sections.technical: SMS phishing sent to employees of at least a dozen companies between 2021 and 2023, with phishing kits capturing credentials relayed to a Telegram channel. Stolen access was used for SIM-swap attacks to intercept SMS and call two-factor codes and take over crypto accounts.
sections.unknown: Which cryptocurrencies were stolen was not specified. The wider Scattered Spider group's status was not addressed in the sources read.

analysis.title: Supply-chain access via trusted platforms
analysis.text: The Optimizely and Microsoft Agent Framework incidents both involved attackers reaching customers through a trusted vendor channel (an experimentation platform, a package registry) rather than the victims' own systems. Optimizely attributes its incident to a signup-flow flaw that let the attacker impersonate administrators; Microsoft has not said how publishing access was obtained.
